items.bio: ceo @box - your business lives in content. unleash it with AI
items.summary_en:
If you were wondering how powerful AI is getting, Agents are now capable of escaping out of systems, finding their way to the internet, discovering zero day security vulnerabilities along the way, and then breaking into external systems - all in an attempt to complete their goal.

Ironically, the ultimate way we’re going to defend against these new risks is equally by throwing compute (in the form of AI) at our code bases, networks, and other systems. You’re going to want vastly more AI on the side of defense as you do on the side of offense. 

We’re entering a new era of what’s going to be possible with AI. Wild times ahead.
items.summary_zh: AI Agent 已经强到能逃出系统、接入互联网、顺手挖出零日漏洞并攻入外部系统，只为完成目标。讽刺的是，防守这类风险的终极办法也是往代码库、网络和系统里砸更多 AI 算力：防守侧的 AI 必须比进攻侧更多。

items.author: Andrej Karpathy
items.bio: I like training large deep neural nets.
items.summary_en: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.
items.summary_zh:
和 LLM 协作时，别总憋着写精确提示词；直接开语音胡乱讲 10 分钟，把脑子里的混乱全倒出来，模型反而擅长从废话里还原你的真实意图。

这种“长篇胡扯”能把人机对齐做得更深，后面少改很多。

items.author: Madhu Guru
items.bio: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
items.summary_en:
The more I’ve relied on my second brain, the dumber my main brain has become.

I’m realizing there’s tremendous value in carrying around a lot of facts, half-baked ideas, and loose threads in your head.

Your subconscious keeps cooking. It makes connections between ideas, extends them, and generates new ones. 

You also have much better real-time recall during conversations, which lets you connect ideas and think faster.

I believe there’s value in a second brain. figuring out how to use one without my main brain getting weaker.
items.summary_zh: 越依赖“第二大脑”，自己的主脑反而越废；脑子里随身带着事实、半成品想法和线头，潜意识才会继续煮、继续连。关键不是不要第二大脑，而是别把它用成主脑的退化器。
